To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
smart cities require a holistic framework for monitoring, analyzing and transforming the urban environment.
smart cities are enabled by ubiquitous sensing and data analytics.

the smart city process can be formalized as a set of five steps, which are: (i) specifying a problem; (ii) monitoring the problem and its context; (iii) analyzing the problem and its causes; (iv) resolving the problem; and (v) transforming the problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conceptualization, development and implementation of smart city frameworks and platforms that are capable of supporting resilient and sustainable urban development.
the development and demonstration of a comprehensive and scalable framework for smart and resilient cities.
the development of an integrated framework for the conceptualization and design of smart cities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology provides a process-oriented framework for conceptualizing and implementing smart cities.
the DICES and SMART frameworks are useful in conceptualizing smart cities and in developing process-oriented methodologies for the same.
smart cities are about the ability to make informed decisions based on evidence, and this is enabled by the ability to monitor and analyze the environment in a systematic and holistic way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
smart cities are about data, insights and evidence, and the process to derive the latter from the former.
the DICES framework is a conceptualization for smart cities, and the SMART methodology is a process-oriented framework to operationalize smart cities.
the DICES and SMART frameworks provide the necessary structure and guidance to enable the creation of a resilient smart city.
The main takeaway from our work is that
smart city is not just a set of technological tools, but a process of continuous monitoring, analysis and decision-making to optimize performance, outcome and resilience of the city.
a comprehensive framework and methodology for smart cities should focus on the processes that enable smartness and resilience.
smart cities are a process and not a technology.
